summary: Minhaj al-Muslim ('The Path of the Muslim') by Shaykh Abu Bakr Jabir al-Jaza'iri (1921–2018 CE) is one of the most widely used contemporary Islamic encyclopedias covering the complete way of life for a Muslim: belief, worship, manners, and dealings. Written in accessible Arabic and widely translated, it serves as a comprehensive practical guide rooted in classical fiqh and Athari aqeedah.
overview:
Minhaj al-Muslim ('The Path of the Muslim') by the Algerian scholar Shaykh Abu Bakr Jabir al-Jaza'iri (1339–1439 AH / 1921–2018 CE) is a comprehensive encyclopedic guide to Islamic life compiled for the modern Muslim reader. Al-Jaza'iri taught for decades at the Prophet's Mosque (Masjid al-Nabawi) in Madinah and produced this work as a practical reference covering every major dimension of a Muslim's daily and spiritual life.

The book is organised into five major sections: (1) Aqeedah (creed), covering the six pillars of faith and the correct Islamic understanding of God's attributes, prophethood, and the unseen; (2) Akhlaq (character and ethics), covering the key virtues and vices, relationships, and social conduct; (3) Ibadah (worship), covering purity, prayer, fasting, zakah, and pilgrimage with rulings from the four schools; (4) Mu'amalat (dealings), covering marriage, divorce, trade, inheritance, and contracts; and (5) Seerah, a brief biographical account of the Prophet ﷺ.

Al-Jaza'iri's approach is Athari in aqeedah, citing the Quran and Sunnah as primary authorities and following the Salaf al-Salih in matters of belief. In fiqh, he synthesises the four Sunni madhabs, noting their positions without exclusive adherence to one school — an approach aimed at the broad Muslim readership he sought to reach.

The book has been translated into English by Darussalam under the title 'Minhaj Al Muslim: The Way of the Muslim' in two volumes, and into numerous other languages. It is one of the most assigned texts in Islamic studies programmes globally and is regularly recommended as a household Islamic reference. Its combination of doctrinal clarity, comprehensive scope, and accessible style makes it a bridge between classical scholarship and the contemporary reader.
